title: Monster Beverage Is Gaining Market Share in the Energy Drink Category
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
summary: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA asks whether Monster Beverage's 20% revenue growth and US/international share gains make it a buy. Revenue has tripled since 2017 to $9.2 billion and ROIC has recovered to 26%, but operating margin has compressed from 38% to 29%, forward P/E 34.6 sits near its high, and his raised DCF of just over $37 remains below the $45+ price — slightly overvalued. He reiterates HOLD (his 1 July stance; first tracked): not a buy here, not worth dumping either. He closes by naming Celsius the better buying opportunity in the category — CELH BUY reiterated as a side mention.

calls.price_at_call: Over $45 (stated current); his DCF a little over $37
calls.thesis: HOLD reiterated (his 1 Jul stance, reiterated here; first tracked, no flip): not a buying opportunity at these levels, but not expensive enough to dump — sit tight and wait for a better entry. Forward P/E 34.6 is near its late-2023 high, and his raised DCF (~$37 vs $45+) still says slightly overvalued.
calls.base_case: Monster keeps gaining share in US and international energy drinks; revenue has tripled since 2017 to $9.2B trailing and growth re-accelerated to 20% YoY last quarter.
calls.bull_case: ROIC has recovered from 16% (2023) to 26%, roughly 2-3x WACC, so reinvestment still creates value.
calls.bear_case: Growth is bought with margin: operating margin has fallen from 38% to 29%, so revenue rises while profitability per sale shrinks.

calls.thesis: BUY reiterated as a closing side mention (was BUY 2026-09-30; no flip): in the energy-drink category he prefers Celsius to Monster — growth is less explosive and SKU/supply-chain management still struggles, but the risk/reward is more attractive.
calls.bear_case: Still struggling with supply-chain and SKU management (his stated caveat).
